ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic дѣтѧ (dětę), from Proto-Slavic *dětę. The и of the first syllable in the singular is from дити́на (ditína), nowadays written дети́на (detína) by analogy with the accented де́ти (déti), with regular distant assimilation ѣ…и́ > и…и́. An alternative formulation by Šakhmatov (ѣ > и before a soft consonant) explains these forms more directly. Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁(y)-, whence also де́ва (déva), дои́ть (doítʹ), Latin fētus, fīlius, fēcundus, fēmina, fēlīx, and many more. Compare typologically сосуно́к (sosunók).
